subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. Close study of one thin, dark 1860s armoured telegraph cable lying slack across pale Atlantic ooze. A deep-sea star next to it establishes scale. Seen in a pool of light from a passing vessel; in the distance the slender line vanishes over a low rise. No thick modern plastic piping, wires or text.
